output.brief:
The October night premium shortfalls were not caused by Fenmarch's data. They trace to one rule change. On 22 Oct, an Ardentra consultant applied a template to the night premium rule (NSP-02). That moved the start of the premium window from 20:00 to 22:00. It was logged as a label correction with "no calc impact" and was not tested. The platform's audit trail can't be edited, and it shows this was the only pay-rule edit. Internal audit recalculated pay for all 158 night workers. 147 were underpaid, and each shortfall equals the 20:00–22:00 premium hours. The 11 staff on 22:00–06:00 shifts were paid correctly. Flagged records were underpaid no more often than unflagged ones. Re-running October with the window set back to 20:00 matched expected pay for all 158. I'm confident in this. Release 7.4, the bank file and timesheet hours are ruled out.

Next steps:
- Have Ardentra restore the 20:00 start and prove it in the test tenant.
- Pay all 147 underpaid staff off-cycle before 24 Nov.
- Don't suspend the HR team, run a full re-cleanse, or accept the clause 14.3 cost on Ardentra's account. Don't roll back 7.4.
- Check the cost of the error against the contract.
- The fall in night overtime cover is mixed up with the rota trial. Fix the pay first, then see whether cover recovers before deciding on the trial.
